lines.text: Honey, you don't drink coffee.

I do when I've been up half the night worrying about a project that's only 1/3 done. And I still have an apron to sew, scenery to paint, plus my normal crushing workload. So unless you have a better way for me to stimulate.

glossary.easy: 감당하기 힘들 만큼 어마어마하게 많은 일
glossary.nuance: 그냥 'a lot of work'보다 훨씬 강하다 — 눌려 짓이겨질(crush) 정도라는 과장된 느낌.
glossary.when: 일이 너무 많아 지칠 때, 회사·학교 일정이 빡빡할 때.
glossary.ex: She quit because of the crushing workload.
glossary.exKo: 그녀는 살인적인 업무량 때문에 회사를 그만뒀다.
glossary.vs: heavy workload는 '많다' 정도지만, crushing workload는 '버티기 힘들다'는 감정까지 담는다.
glossary.tip: crushing은 '으스러뜨리는'이라는 형용사로, 부담·패배(crushing defeat) 같은 데도 자주 쓴다.

lines.text: God. Coffee's bitter.
That was your first sip.
Okay, I got the chafing dish.
Salt and pepper shakers. Perfect.
Matches both. I may have to readjust my grapes.
Oh, well, I'll just give you a little privacy.
Welcome back to the light show.
Hi.
Hi, Lily.
Hi, daddy.
Lily, sweetheart. No no no no no, we're we're not going to do that.
Actually, actually, Claire, we're trying not to use the word no so much.
We just read a book that said children learn to rebel against that word.
So we redirect her into a new activity instead.

glossary.easy: 규칙이나 시키는 사람에게 일부러 맞서고 따르지 않다
glossary.nuance: 단순히 'NO'가 아니라, 권위·통제에 대놓고 저항하는 느낌.
glossary.when: 사춘기 아이가 부모 말을 안 들을 때, 시민이 정부에 저항할 때.
glossary.ex: Teenagers often rebel against their parents' rules.
glossary.vs: disobey는 그냥 '안 따르다'지만, rebel against는 '맞서 싸우다'에 가깝다.

glossary.easy: 가던 방향이나 쏠린 관심을 다른 쪽으로 바꿔주다
glossary.nuance: 막는 게 아니라 '방향만 틀어' 흘려보내는 부드러운 느낌.
glossary.when: 떼쓰는 아이의 주의를 장난감으로 돌릴 때, 대화 주제를 바꿀 때.
glossary.ex: She redirected the child's attention to a toy.
glossary.tip: re(다시) + direct(향하게 하다) = 방향을 다시 잡아주다, 로 외우면 쉽다.

lines.text: We'll just watch this. Lily, sweetie.
Hi. It's daddy here. Would you like to listen to some music?
Okay. There you go. You see?
Every new generation thinks they have cracked the code on child rearing.

glossary.easy: 아무도 못 풀던 어려운 문제의 답·비결을 드디어 알아내다
glossary.nuance: 암호(code)를 풀듯, 한참 헤매다 '아하!' 하고 핵심을 간파한 느낌.
glossary.when: 오래 고민하던 문제의 해법을 찾았을 때, 성공 비결을 깨달았을 때.
glossary.ex: After years of trying, they finally cracked the code on customer retention.
glossary.exKo: 몇 년을 시도한 끝에 그들은 마침내 고객 유지의 비결을 알아냈다.
glossary.tip: crack은 '깨다/금이 가다'지만, crack the code는 통째로 '비밀을 풀다'라는 관용구다.

glossary.easy: 아이를 먹이고 가르치며 어른으로 키워내는 모든 과정
glossary.nuance: 단순 돌봄보다 '제대로 길러낸다'는 양육의 무게가 담긴 말.
glossary.when: 육아 방식, 자녀 교육을 진지하게 이야기할 때.
glossary.ex: Child rearing is a full-time responsibility.
glossary.exKo: 육아는 잠시도 쉴 수 없는 책임이다.
glossary.vs: babysitting은 잠깐 봐주는 것, child rearing은 오랜 기간 길러내는 것.

lines.text: What's the latest theory? Never say no.
I say no every day in this house.
But at night, she's a yes machine.
No.

Do you see how she's slowly transitioning from the lights to the music?
Yeah, I do. It's hard to believe there was ever a time when we just said, stop doing that. Oh, the garbage disposal.
Lily. No no no no no no no no no no.

Actually, we're doing this new thing where we let her tell us when she wants to take a nap.
It's called being your own nap captain.

Okay, this is way too many grapes.

So if we use it, everyone at the table has to react in shock at the spoon from the future.

You need a nap.
I got it. Oh, I lost it. Shoot.
Let me know if I can eliminate any distractions for you.
Oh, I got it. No, I got a finger on it. There it is. Oh. Lost it again.
Maybe you should just wait until it comes to you. You know, make it the captain of its own spoon platoon.
I understand the point you're making, Claire, but. Oh, now I'm stuck.
Yeah, Cam, you are stuck. You are stuck on a philosophy that clearly doesn't work.
Sometimes you need to say no to a child.
Yeah, and sometimes you need to say no to an adult.
No, Claire. No. I don't need help raising my child.
Oh, okay. I'm sorry. Oh. I guess I do have a lot to learn. Right now I'm looking forward to learning if you will get your arm out of there before Lily gets to the garbage disposal switch.
Um. Lily, sweetie. Can you do something, please Claire?
I would like to. Really, I would, but I would probably just say no and shred her confidence and mangle her self-esteem.
Okay, fine. I'm sorry. Just hear. Just stop her. Stop her.
Stop her. Sweetie. Claire!
Okay.
Oh.
Yes.
Oh. Oh, you think that's funny, don't you?
Yes.
It's wicked, Claire. It's wicked.
Come on, we're leaving Lily!
Lily!
